# Morning gurgle cooling air trap noise

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Elevate front end, wait for pressure loss, remove caps, fill coolant while cranking, and squeeze hose until bubbles vanish. [t501]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Park the truck on ramps or patio stones to elevate the front end.
2. [Partial] Wait until the cooling system loses pressure (allowing time for a meal, TV show, or nap).
3. Remove caps from both the radiator and overflow tank, ensuring the overflow cap has a spring mechanism.
4. Fill the radiator with coolant while cranking the engine to circulate fluid through it.
5. [Partial] Squeeze the upper radiator hose repeatedly until bubbles appear in the fill neck.
6. Repeat filling and squeezing until no more bubbles are noticed.

_Procedure reported by [t501]._

## Tools

- [Partial] Mechanic ramps or patio stones [t501]

## Tips & gotchas

- Verify the radiator is filled properly before installing the final cap. [t501]
- Check fluid levels in the overflow tank after driving to ensure it remains topped off. [t501]
